sources.quote: 8.1% of psychiatrists have opted out of Medicare, followed by 4.5% of physicians specializing in plastic and reconstructive surgery and 3.2% of physicians specializing in neurology.
sources.searcher_note: Opt-out rates by specialty and state, from the same CMS opt-out affidavit file, but physicians only. Says nothing about family therapists, social workers or psychologists; top states named are DC, Alaska, Colorado, Idaho, not California.

notes: No source found gives a Medicare opt-out rate for family therapists (MFTs), in California or anywhere, or compares MFTs with social workers or psychologists. What turned up is explainers and how-to pages (CAMFT newsletters, practice blogs, CMS FAQ, Axios Dec 2023) saying MFTs became Medicare-eligible Jan 1, 2024, get paid 75% of the psychologist rate, and must either enroll or opt out. Those are explainers, not findings, so they aren't recorded. The only finding-level pattern source is KFF on physician opt-out (psychiatrists 8.1%). A JGIM study on psychiatrist opt-out by state (Springer, 2019) redirected to a login wall and wasn't recorded. Nothing found dated after 2026-06-30.
